I can't run the simulator here, so this ranking comes from hand analysis of the bias network and the power budget.

Power is the clearest clue. Tracing the currents from the mirrors (M4 ≈ 4.76·I_ref, M6 ≈ 2.13·I_ref, M7 = I_ref) gives about 7.9·I_ref total, so the 133 µW measurement implies I_ref ≈ 9 µA. The M4/M7 ratio of 2/0.42 is the largest multiplier in the design, and it feeds the pb node that sets the first-stage current through M3/M2. An error there would both overshoot power and distort the first stage's gm, which is consistent with the bandwidth failure (3.2 MHz vs. 23 MHz). M3 and M6 are the next most likely, since they set the same bias chain and the output-follower current.

I can't uniquely identify the fault from these numbers, so treat this as a ranked hypothesis to confirm by re-simulating the candidates with their nominal sizes.

This overshoots total power (~133 uW vs 94 uW) and shifts the pb bias that sets the first-stage current, which is consistent with the low f3dB. Restoring the nominal W/L of M4 should bring power and bandwidth back in spec."}
